 Aparna Yadav Urges Akhilesh to Accept Mathura Invitation, Says Ram and Krishna Are Matters of Faith, Not Politics
 Uttar Pradesh State Commission for Women Vice-Chairperson Aparna Yadav has said that Lord Ram and Lord Krishna are matters of faith and should not be turned into election issues. Reacting to Deputy C…
 Published By : 
 Dheeraj Singh , Kanpur 
 Last Updated: November 19, 2026, 18:30 IST 
 Aparna Yadav comments on the Mathura invitation and the Ram and Krishna temple issue. 
 Uttar Pradesh State Commission for Women Vice-Chairperson Aparna Yadav has said that Lord Ram and Lord Krishna are matters of faith and should not be turned into election issues. Reacting to Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya's invitation to Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav to visit Mathura, she described the gesture as a positive initiative and urged the former chief minister to accept the invitation.
 Aparna made the remarks while speaking to reporters in Kanpur on November 19, amid growing political discussion around the Krishna Janmasthan temple in Mathura ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections.
 Ram and Krishna Are Matters of Faith, Says Aparna
 Aparna said Lord Ram and Lord Krishna are deeply revered and will always remain central to the faith of devotees. She described the construction of the Ram temple in Ayodhya as essential from the perspective of Sanatan Dharma.
 Referring to the Krishna temple in Mathura, she said the temple already existed and that the government had decided some time ago to improve it further.
 She appealed to people not to turn religious deities and places of worship into subjects of electoral politics. According to her, these matters should be viewed through the lens of faith and devotion rather than political competition.
 Akhilesh Should Accept Keshav Maurya's Mathura Invitation
 Reacting to Keshav Prasad Maurya's invitation to Akhilesh Yadav to visit Mathura, Aparna called it a good initiative.
 She said invitations of this kind are extended to promote Sanatan culture and religion, adding that those who have been invited should accept them willingly.
 Maurya's invitation has drawn attention because the Mathura temple issue has increasingly featured in political statements by BJP leaders ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections.
 Aparna Comments on Election Slogans and Posters
 Aparna was also asked about the BJP's election slogans and posters. She said political slogans are used during election campaigns to generate enthusiasm among the public.
 Her remarks came alongside her appeal to keep religious matters separate from electoral politics, bringing attention to the debate over how faith-related issues are discussed during political campaigns.
 Seeks Strict Action Over Minor's Death During PDA Roadshow
 Aparna also responded to the death of a minor student during a PDA roadshow in Gorakhpur. Describing the incident as unfortunate, she said strict action should be taken against whoever is found responsible.
 She maintained that accountability should not depend on political affiliation. If anyone is found responsible for an incident during a rally or political programme, action should follow.
 She also said the Women's Commission would make efforts to ensure that those responsible are held accountable.
 Mathura Issue Remains in Focus Ahead of 2027 UP Elections
 With the next Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections approaching, statements around Ayodhya and Mathura have become increasingly prominent in the state's political discourse.
 Keshav Prasad Maurya's invitation to Akhilesh Yadav and Aparna Yadav's response have added another development to the ongoing discussion.
 Aparna has emphasised that religious faith should not be reduced to an electoral contest. Attention will now turn to Akhilesh Yadav's response to the invitation and how the Mathura issue develops in the coming months.
